collection: NERDC JSS 1 Intermediate Science woodwork and metalwork hand tools
note: Original structured practice with manual marking guides. Independent academic review pending.

questions.subject: Intermediate Science
questions.topic: Machines and Tools: Woodwork Hand Tools
questions.learningObjective: Classify woodwork hand tools by their main function.
questions.prompt: A bench tray contains a steel rule, a tenon saw and a G-cramp. Match each tool to the job it is designed for: measuring stock, cutting wood or holding work steady.
questions.answer: The steel rule measures stock. The tenon saw cuts wood. The G-cramp holds work steady.
questions.explanation: The groups describe what the tools do during the job.

markingGuide.description: Matches the steel rule to measuring.
Matches the tenon saw to cutting.
Matches the G-cramp to holding.

questions.subject: Intermediate Science
questions.topic: Machines and Tools: Woodwork Hand Tools
questions.learningObjective: Explain how a marking gauge produces a line at a constant offset from a straight edge.
questions.prompt: A carpenter shows a marked line running 12 mm from a straight board edge. On the marking gauge, which part follows the edge and which part makes the line? Explain why the gap stays constant.
questions.answer: The stock or fence follows the edge. The pin makes the mark. The distance from the fence to the pin stays fixed when the gauge is locked.
questions.explanation: The fence uses the board edge as a reference for the position of the pin.

markingGuide.description: Identifies the stock or fence.
Identifies the marking pin.
Explains how a fixed setting maintains the offset.

questions.subject: Intermediate Science
questions.topic: Machines and Tools: Woodwork Hand Tools
questions.subtopic: Selecting a clamp for a glue-up
questions.learningObjective: Explain why a clamp must have sufficient working capacity.
questions.prompt: A project panel is 45 cm wide. A G-cramp in the tray can open to 15 cm and a sash cramp can open to 60 cm. Which tool can span the panel across its width, and why?
questions.answer: The 60 cm sash cramp can span 45 cm. The 15 cm G-cramp cannot open wide enough.
questions.explanation: The deciding dimension is the usable gap between the jaws.

markingGuide.description: Selects the sash cramp.
Compares the openings with the panel width.

questions.subject: Intermediate Science
questions.topic: Machines and Tools: Woodwork Hand Tools
questions.subtopic: Mallet and hammer in an assembly
questions.learningObjective: Describe a reason to choose an appropriate driving tool for a task.
questions.prompt: A teacher is assembling a fitted wooden joint without nails. Explain why a wooden mallet and a scrap wood pad could be suitable for settling the pieces together.
questions.answer: A wooden mallet delivers controlled taps. A pad spreads the contact and protects the visible surface from direct blows and dents.
questions.explanation: The choice depends on the material and the finish the worker wants to preserve.

markingGuide.description: Explains why a mallet is suitable.
Explains how the pad protects the surface.

questions.subject: Intermediate Science
questions.topic: Machines and Tools: Woodwork Hand Tools
questions.subtopic: Returning tools after a damp lesson
questions.learningObjective: Explain a routine to protect woodwork hand tools after use.
questions.prompt: At the end of a workshop lesson, a steel rule is damp and a tenon saw has loose sawdust on it. Describe how the tools should be prepared and stored.
questions.answer: Dry the rule and remove loose sawdust from the saw using the teacher-approved cleaning method. Return the rule flat and the saw to its designated rack with its teeth protected.
questions.explanation: Dry, protected storage reduces corrosion and prevents tools being knocked together.

markingGuide.description: States that the damp rule should be dried.
Describes suitable saw cleaning.
Gives protected storage for both tools.

questions.subject: Intermediate Science
questions.topic: Machines and Tools: Metalwork Hand Tools
questions.subtopic: Identifying a tool for a fine line
questions.learningObjective: Identify the metalwork tool used to mark a line on sheet metal.
questions.prompt: A technician needs to mark a fine line on a flat metal specimen. The tray contains a scriber, a spanner and a file. Which is intended to mark the line? Give one feature that suits it to the job.
questions.answer: The scriber. Its hard pointed tip can make a fine visible mark on suitable metal.
questions.explanation: A scriber transfers layout information to the material's surface.

markingGuide.description: Identifies the scriber.
Links its pointed tip to making a fine line.

questions.subject: Intermediate Science
questions.topic: Machines and Tools: Metalwork Hand Tools
questions.learningObjective: Explain the importance of choosing a correctly fitting spanner.
questions.prompt: A pupil at a supervised bench finds that the open-ended spanner rocks from side to side on a hexagonal nut. What should the pupil check before using it and what problem would that prevent?
questions.answer: Check that the spanner size fits the nut closely. A loose fit can slip or damage the corners of the nut.
questions.explanation: Correct fit lets the jaws engage the nut's flats securely.

markingGuide.description: States that the spanner should fit the nut closely.
Explains the risk of slipping or rounding the corners.

questions.subject: Intermediate Science
questions.topic: Machines and Tools: Metalwork Hand Tools
questions.subtopic: Distinguishing tools by the marks they leave
questions.learningObjective: Describe different purposes of a centre punch and a file.
questions.prompt: Two specimens show different workshop operations. One has a small indentation exactly where a hole is planned. On the other, a rough projecting burr has been smoothed. Which tool is associated with each operation: centre punch or file?
questions.answer: A centre punch makes the starting indentation. A file removes material to smooth the burr.
questions.explanation: The punch makes a local mark, while the file removes small amounts from an edge or surface.

markingGuide.description: Matches the centre punch to the indentation.
Matches the file to smoothing the burr.

questions.subject: Intermediate Science
questions.topic: Machines and Tools: Metalwork Hand Tools
questions.learningObjective: Draw a recognisable labelled sketch of a metalwork hand tool.
questions.prompt: From a teacher-provided example, sketch an open-ended spanner on paper. Label the jaws and the handle. Add one sentence explaining what the opening fits.
questions.answer: A suitable sketch shows a handle ending in two jaws with an open gap. The opening fits across opposite flats of a suitably sized nut or bolt head.
questions.explanation: The visible jaw opening distinguishes an open-ended spanner from a ring spanner.

markingGuide.description: Produces a recognisable open-ended profile.
Labels jaws and handle correctly.
Explains what the opening fits.

questions.subject: Intermediate Science
questions.topic: Machines and Tools: Metalwork Hand Tools
questions.learningObjective: Explain how cleaning and storing a file preserve its cutting surface.
questions.prompt: A metalwork file has small filings trapped among its teeth. Identify a suitable cleaning tool and explain how to store the file afterwards so its cutting surface is protected.
questions.answer: Use a file card or suitable file brush under the teacher's direction. Store the file dry in its own slot or sleeve so its teeth do not rub against other tools.
questions.explanation: Removing trapped particles lets the teeth work properly. Keeping tools apart protects their working surfaces.

markingGuide.description: Identifies a file card or suitable file brush.
Describes separate, dry storage.
Explains how either action protects performance.
